name: clear_serial_status_and_notify
description: Clears bit 6 of a status byte in the serial unit record and, when that bit was set and a global counter is zero, sets bit 2 of the record's flag byte, stores the current buffer pointer if its slot is empty, and calls the library function at offset minus 180.

name: receive_serial_byte_into_buffer
description: Masks the incoming serial word with a stored mask and, depending on the unit's flags, either stores the byte into the receive buffer and advances its pointer and count, or treats a matching special character as an event and sets the matching status flag. It ends by calling a library function through the library base.

name: set_serial_ready_flag_notify
description: Sets bit 0 of the serial unit status byte, stores the current buffer pointer in an empty slot if needed, and calls the library function at offset minus 180 to signal the event.

name: queue_or_start_serial_request
description: Clears the pending bit on a request record and, when the unit counters are zero, makes the request current and writes the interrupt control word; otherwise it appends the request to a waiting list when a unit flag is set. It then passes control to the flag-check routine.

name: start_serial_request_or_wait
description: Checks the unit's active-transfer flag and, if a request is already attached, either passes control to the flag-check routine or returns; otherwise it marks the request as active, records it as the current request, and writes the interrupt enable word twice.

name: return_immediately
description: Does nothing and returns at once; the executable references its address only as a handler pointer, so it has no behaviour of its own.

name: set_carriage_return_terminator
description: When the global control word has bit 3 set and bit 3 or bit 4 set in the word, it writes character 13 into the unit record byte at offset 31, marking a carriage return as the end of a line.

name: service_serial_transmit_queue
description: Handles one serial transmit step: it checks abort and wait flags, takes the next byte from the current request buffer, and writes it with the saved control bits to the serial data register. When the request is finished or times out it detaches it from the queue, moves to the next waiting request, and calls the library function.

name: transmit_next_serial_byte
description: Resets the timeout counter to 200, writes the next byte from the current transmit buffer to the serial data register with the saved control bits, and advances the buffer pointer and count. Once the count reaches its limit it completes the request through the library function.

name: transmit_serial_byte_when_due
description: Compares the transfer count against a limit held in a register and, while the transfer is still in progress, writes the next byte with the saved control bits to the serial data register and advances the buffer and count. Otherwise it completes the request through the library function.

name: write_serial_data_and_advance
description: Finishes a serial transmit step by setting an extra bit when the zero flag is clear, combining the byte with the saved control word, and writing it to the serial data register. It advances the transfer counters and completes the request through the library function once the limit is reached.

name: dequeue_next_serial_request
description: If requests are waiting, removes the first one from the queue, decrements the pending count, and makes it the current request with its counters reset; it starts that request when its type code is ten. With nothing waiting it writes 1 to the global control word.

name: disable_serial_interrupts
description: Writes the value 1 to the global control word, which without the enable bit clears the serial interrupt bits, and returns.

name: send_pending_control_character
description: Disables the interrupt control word, takes the pending control byte from the unit record and clears it, then writes it combined with the saved control word. It returns early, leaving the control word disabled, when no current or queued request exists.

name: reset_serial_unit_defaults
description: Aborts any active or waiting requests and clears the unit status, then stores several default configuration constants into the unit record, including a timing value of 250000. It finishes by enabling the serial interrupt control word and calling the library function when the status allows.

name: signal_library_after_state_copy
description: Runs the state-copy routine on the unit record, then calls the library function at offset minus 378 when the record's flag bits under mask 81 are clear.

name: flag_and_signal_serial_request
description: Sets a pending-completion bit on the unit record when a request is attached, runs the flag-check routine when a second pointer is set, and calls the library function at offset minus 378 when the request's flag bits are clear.

name: clear_flag_and_enable_serial
description: Clears the pending-completion bit on the unit record, runs the flag-check routine when a second pointer is set, and writes the enable word to turn serial interrupts back on. It then calls the library function at offset minus 378 when the request flags are clear.

name: reset_serial_interrupt_control
description: Disables serial interrupts by writing the control word with a fixed bit pattern, clears the serial flag through a helper routine, and then re-enables them with the enable bit set. It calls the library function at offset minus 378 when the request flags are clear.

name: drain_serial_request_list
description: Repeatedly removes the first node from the linked list whose head pointer is passed in and passes each node to the flag-setting routine, until the list is empty.

name: return_without_action
description: Does nothing and returns at once; the executable reaches it only through a handler pointer, so it has no behaviour of its own.

name: capture_serial_line_status
description: Captures the input line status bits from a hardware port register into the request record, copies the unit's current transfer position into it, and clears two pending flags on the unit. It calls the library function at offset minus 378 when the record's flag bits under mask 81 are clear.

name: queue_request_or_activate_next
description: Clears the pending bit on the request and, if it is flagged while the unit already has an active or queued request, appends it to the waiting list and signals the library. Otherwise it passes the request to the flag-check routine, then makes it the current request and enables the interrupt bits, or signals the library and clears the current request.

name: activate_request_or_signal
description: Passes the request to the flag-check routine, then either makes it the current request with the transmit-ready flag set and enables serial interrupts, or signals the library and clears the current request.

name: signal_library_and_clear_request
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 378 and then clears the unit's current request pointer.

name: complete_request_and_restore_interrupts
description: Clears the active-transfer bit on the request and, when that bit was set and the request type is ten, clears the current request, disables serial interrupts and signals the library. It then writes the enable word to restore interrupts.

name: configure_serial_timer_request
description: Disables interrupts, stores a zero, the value passed in a register and the count 9 into the unit's request fields, then calls a library function through a pointer. It marks the request with character 11 when a status byte is set and returns the library result with its low byte cleared.

name: update_request_abort_state
description: Updates the unit's request-state flags from the top flag bit of the record, and when no transfer is active it toggles the interrupt control word off and on; otherwise it marks the record with status code 1. It calls the library function at offset minus 378 when the record's flag bits are clear.

name: clear_flag_and_restart_interrupts
description: Clears the unit's top flag bit and, when no transfer is pending, toggles the serial interrupt control word off and on; otherwise it marks the record with status code 1. It then calls the library function at offset minus 378 when the record's flag bits are clear.

name: pulse_interrupt_control_around_check
description: Disables serial interrupts, runs the flag-check routine on the record and then re-enables them, calling the library function at offset minus 378 when the record's flag bits are clear.

name: validate_and_apply_serial_config
description: Checks that three configuration bytes and a timing value fall within fixed bounds and that a buffer pointer is set. When the checks pass it copies the parameters into the unit record, sets the matching flags and recalculates the timing; otherwise it writes an error code into the record.

name: compute_serial_bit_masks
description: Builds a bit mask from the record's bit-position byte, widening it when the second configuration byte is two and shifting it left when the unit's flag bit is set. It stores the mask and two computed values in the unit record.

name: set_serial_error_code_five
description: Writes status code 5 into the request record's status byte at offset 31 and returns.

name: compute_serial_clock_divider
description: Divides the constant 25000000 by the stored rate value multiplied by seven to get a 16-bit divider, scaling the result when the value is too large. It writes the divider to the serial period register and sets the unit's flags when the configuration byte equals eight and flag bit 1 is set.

name: divide_serial_clock_period
description: Divides a 32-bit value by a 16-bit divisor passed in registers, stores the quotient in the unit record and writes it to the serial period register. It then updates the unit's flags the same way the other timing routine does, setting a bit when the configuration byte equals eight and flag bit 1 is set.

name: initialise_serial_unit_resources
description: Allocates a serial unit record through a library function and, on success, stores the owner and device base in it, sets a default timeout of 200, claims the miscellaneous resource and initialises its queues and handler pointers. It returns one when setup succeeds and zero otherwise.

name: initialise_serial_unit_queues
description: Sets up the unit's two request queues, stores their status bytes and list pointers, installs the handler pointers and calls a library function to finish setup. It returns one.

name: fill_serial_request_node
description: Stores the link pointer into the request node, sets its type code to 16, and writes the address of the global variable together with two register values into node fields.

name: setup_serial_request_block
description: Sets up the serial unit's queues and handler pointers as the other setup routines do, enables a device request through a library call at offset minus 162, and leaves serial interrupts disabled by writing the control word.

name: return_zero_status
description: Returns zero without doing any other work, reporting no result to its caller.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The entry in the keymap file decodes only to bad data, not to code, so there is no routine behaviour to recover.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The entry in the sound data file decodes only to bad data, not to code, so there is no routine behaviour to recover.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The entry in the sound data file decodes only to bad data, not to code, so there is no routine behaviour to recover.

name: increment_counter_clear_flag_bit
description: Adds one to a 16-bit counter at offset 32 of the structure in the base register and clears bit 3 of the flags byte at offset 14. This is icon library code.

name: decrement_counter_and_release
description: Subtracts one from the 16-bit counter at offset 32. When the counter reaches zero and flag bit 3 is set, it calls another routine and returns that result, otherwise it returns zero. This is icon library code.

name: unlink_node_when_count_zero
description: When the 16-bit value at offset 8 is zero, it calls the library function at offset minus 210 and removes the node from its linked list, returning the call's result. Otherwise it sets flag bit 3 in the flags byte and returns zero.

name: set_flag_bit_return_zero
description: Sets bit 3 of the flags byte at offset 14 of the structure and returns zero. This is icon library code.

name: return_zero_without_work
description: Returns zero and does nothing else. This is icon library code.

name: open_library_and_store_base
description: Stores two caller-supplied values in the structure, calls a library function at offset minus 552 and keeps the base it returns. On failure it calls the system alert routine; on success it copies the two stored values into two global variables.

name: copy_two_values_to_globals
description: Copies two 32-bit values from offsets 34 and 38 of the structure in an address register into two global variables. This is icon library code.

name: invoke_nested_routine_and_return
description: Calls one nested routine and returns with no work of its own; several library dispatch entries reach the same wrapper. The callee is not named in the executable.

name: forward_to_nested_routine

name: store_value_in_returned_record
description: Calls a library function at offset minus 294 with the first argument, then stores the second argument into the returned structure at offset 148. This is icon library code.

name: allocate_and_attach_or_release
description: Calls one routine with the last two arguments to get a result. When the result is nonzero it calls a second routine with the first two arguments and the result; if that fails it releases the result and returns zero, otherwise it returns the result.

name: load_icon_header_into_record
description: Allocates a record, reads a 44-byte header block and a set of 32-bit fields into it through a loader routine, and links it to a parent record when one is set. It returns the record, or zero when allocation or reading fails.

name: copy_icon_header_fields
description: Copies a 44-byte block from a stack buffer into the record at offset 96, then copies a byte and several 32-bit fields from the stack into fixed record offsets. It links the record into its parent when the link field is set.

name: return_zero_without_work
description: Returns zero without any other work. This is icon library code.

name: pack_icon_header_into_buffer
description: Builds a header with a fixed magic value and a version of 1 on the stack, copies the record's 44-byte block and its fields into a stack buffer after it, and passes the buffer to another routine together with the first two arguments.

name: load_icon_file_for_record
description: Builds a file path in a 260-byte buffer using the .info suffix, then checks the header magic word and version number before reading the icon's fields into the record. It returns one on success and zero when the lookup or validation fails.

name: read_icon_optional_sections
description: Checks the header magic word and version number, then reads the record's optional data pointers, allocating and filling their blocks when they are missing. It returns one on success and zero when a read or allocation fails.

name: read_icon_string_list_sections
description: Reads the record's optional string and pointer sections in the same way, with the list entries read until each zero terminator. It returns one on success and zero when any read fails.

name: read_icon_pointer_list_entries
description: Reads 32-bit pointer entries into a list until the count runs out, then reads one more value into the field at offset 70 when that field is set. It returns one on success and zero when a read fails.

name: pass_through_then_return_zero
description: Calls one nested routine and then returns zero.

name: return_immediately
description: Does nothing and returns at once.

name: write_icon_file_for_record
description: Allocates a 260-byte work buffer for building a file path and writes the icon's header, optional sections and lists through a sequence of writer calls. It reports error 103 when the buffer cannot be allocated, frees the buffer and returns zero if any write fails.

name: write_icon_sections_and_header
description: Writes the icon's header value and its optional sections and lists through a sequence of writer calls. It returns one on success and zero if any write fails.

name: write_icon_string_list_sections
description: Writes the record's string and pointer lists, each entry followed by its length, and returns one on success and zero when a write fails.

name: measure_and_write_string_list
description: Measures a zero-terminated list of strings by adding each length plus one to a running total, then writes the list entries and the optional string at offset 70 through the writer. It stores the total in the record at offset 26. This is icon library code.

name: write_string_pointer_list
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of string pointers, writing each entry and its length through the writer, then writes the optional string at offset 70. It stores the running total in the record at offset 26.

name: release_list_nodes
description: Repeatedly takes the node found at offset 2 past the given pointer and passes it to a release routine until no nodes remain.

name: return_immediately
description: Does nothing and returns at once. This is icon library code.

name: forward_call_with_offset_140
description: Calls one routine with the same first argument and the second argument increased by 140, then returns.

name: allocate_icon_record_block
description: Allocates a cleared 168-byte block, initialises a field inside it and runs a setup routine on it with a sub-block. It returns the block on success; when a setup step fails it frees the block and returns zero.

name: pass_through_to_nested_routine
description: Calls one nested routine and returns with no other work of its own. This is icon library code.

name: return_zero_without_work
description: Returns zero without doing anything else. This is icon library code.

name: store_pair_with_refill
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter, asking a refill routine for more entries when the count runs out, then stores two 32-bit values into the next slot of the table and returns one. It returns zero when the refill fails.

name: decrement_counter_and_store_pair
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter and stores two 32-bit values into the table slot the counter now indexes, then returns one.

name: allocate_icon_string_block
description: Allocates a cleared 94-byte block, initialises a field inside it and runs two setup routines on it, returning the block. When a step fails it frees the block and returns zero.

name: return_immediately
description: Does nothing and returns at once. This is icon library code.

name: call_library_then_return_zero
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 210 and then returns zero.

name: forward_call_with_offset_78
description: Calls one routine with the same first argument and the second argument increased by 78, then returns.

name: find_option_value_in_list
description: Searches a zero-terminated list of strings for an entry with the requested key and returns the text after its equals sign, or zero when nothing matches.

name: return_zero_without_work
description: Returns zero without doing anything else. This is icon library code.

name: find_matching_separated_segment
description: Scans a buffer of segments split by separator character 124 for one whose length equals the expected length and whose comparison passes, returning one when it finds one and zero otherwise.

name: search_separated_segments
description: Searches a buffer of segments split by separator character 124 for a matching entry, using the register-based comparison, and returns one when a match is found.

name: search_segments_by_length
description: Scans segments split by separator character 124 for one with the expected length whose comparison passes, returning one on a match and zero when the list ends.

name: scan_separated_segments
description: Walks segments split by separator character 124 and returns one when a segment of the expected length passes the comparison, or zero when none does.

name: return_zero_without_work
description: Returns zero without doing anything else. This is icon library code.

name: parse_copy_name_prefix
description: Checks a name for a 'copy' prefix, reading an optional decimal counter that follows it, and stores the text after the prefix into the record. It returns the record.

name: validate_copy_number_prefix
description: Checks a name for a numbered copy prefix, reads the decimal number after it and confirms the trailing text, returning nothing.

name: parse_decimal_then_match_text
description: Reads decimal digits from a character pointer, then compares the text that follows them with a fixed four-character string and returns when the check finishes.

name: parse_copy_suffix_number
description: Reads a decimal number from a character pointer and checks that the four characters after it match a fixed string, returning nothing. The copy-of format text is referenced here.

name: convert_digit_char_to_value
description: Maps an ASCII character code from 48 to 57 to its digit value from 0 to 9 and returns minus one for any other character.

name: invoke_library_routine_then_return
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 198 through a base pointer kept in the data, then returns.

name: allocate_and_attach_or_release
description: Calls one routine with the last two arguments to get a result. When the result is nonzero it calls a second routine with the first two arguments and the result; if that fails it releases the result and returns zero, otherwise it returns the result.

name: allocate_cleared_block_marked_ten
description: Allocates a cleared 96-byte block, sets a value of 10 in its size field and in the byte the caller supplies, then passes the block to a second routine. It returns true when allocation succeeds.

name: return_zero_without_work
description: Returns zero without doing anything else. This is icon library code.

name: check_library_call_result
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 42 with the last three arguments and returns the last argument when the result equals it, or zero otherwise.

name: return_immediately

name: verify_library_call_outcome
description: Calls the library function at offset minus 48 with the last three arguments and returns the last argument when the result equals it, or zero otherwise.

name: return_immediately
description: Does nothing and returns at once. This is icon library code.

name: divide_unsigned_32bit_values
description: Divides an unsigned 32-bit value by an unsigned divisor passed in registers. It uses a bit-by-bit long division when the divisor is above 65535 and 16-bit division otherwise, and returns the quotient and remainder.

name: divide_32bit_shift_subtract
description: Runs a sixteen-step shift-and-subtract loop on a 32-bit value against a divisor, leaving the quotient and remainder in the registers.

name: multiply_32bit_with_swap
description: Forms the 32-bit product of two register values from 16-bit partial products and returns it together with the second value with its two halves exchanged.

name: call_raw_format_function
description: Calls the library formatting function at offset minus 522 and returns nothing; the referenced text identifies it as the exec formatted-output routine.

name: store_low_byte_at_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the D0 register at the address held in the A3 register.

name: measure_c_string_length
description: Counts the characters of a zero-terminated string up to the terminator and returns that length. This is icon library code.

name: find_char_in_c_string
description: Scans a zero-terminated string for the given character and returns a pointer to its first occurrence, or zero when the string ends first.

name: return_zero_without_work

name: copy_c_string

name: append_c_string

name: compare_c_strings_limited

name: return_one_without_work

name: walk_string_within_limit

name: pass_through_to_nested_routine

name: copy_c_string_padded

name: return_immediately

name: initialise_empty_list_header
description: Sets the first word of a block to point just past itself, clears the next word and stores the block's own address in the third word, forming an empty list header. This is icon library code.

name: process_optional_node_entry
description: Returns one when the pointer argument is zero. Otherwise it runs a routine on a 20-byte block and, if that succeeds, calls two more routines with the value stored at offset 10 of the block, returning the result of that chain.

name: process_linked_entry_list

name: return_one_without_work

name: allocate_cleared_node_block

name: return_minus_one
description: Returns minus one without doing anything else. This is icon library code.

name: allocate_node_chain_from_entries
description: Allocates a chain of cleared 16-byte nodes, each with a counted array of 32-bit entries filled by two routines, and links the nodes through their next-pointer fields. It returns the head node, zero when no nodes are requested, or minus one when a step fails.

name: allocate_node_list_from_entries
description: Builds a list of entries by allocating each node and its array in turn, and returns the head of the list, or minus one when a step fails.

name: return_immediately

name: return_minus_one

name: initialise_library_and_register

name: increment_counter_clear_bit5

name: decrement_counter_and_release_bit5

name: unlink_node_and_signal

name: unlink_node_and_call_library

name: return_low_word_value

name: scan_translation_fields_until_hash

name: scan_translation_until_marker

name: parse_escaped_text_segments

name: scan_backward_word_characters

name: scan_backward_matching_prefix

name: compare_text_until_equals
